chunks: From him, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Yahya ibn al-Mubarak, from 'Abd Allah ibn Jabalah, from Abi Jamilah, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام.
Concerning a slave and a free man who killed a free man, he said:
“If he wishes, he may kill the free man, and if he wishes, he may kill the slave. If he chooses to kill the free man, the two sides of the slave are to be flogged.”

key_terms.جَنْبَا الْعَبْدِ: the two sides of the slave, indicating the location of the flogging
key_terms.جُلِدَ: was flogged as a corporal punishment
key_terms.حُرٍّ: a free person, distinguished legally from a slave in the ruling
key_terms.عَبْدٍ: a slave involved in the homicide case
key_terms.قَتَلَ الْحُرَّ: to execute the free man in retaliation
key_terms.قَتَلَ الْعَبْدَ: to execute the slave in retaliation

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a slave and a free man jointly kill a free man?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning retaliation when a slave and a free man jointly kill a free man. It states that the heir or entitled party may choose to execute either the free man or the slave, and if the free man is executed, the slave is punished by flogging.
